significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that a conserved quantity is encoded as a linear direction whose decoded value has "low within-trajectory variance" and whose ablation harms "long-horizon rollout stability more than short-horizon accuracy." This combines a form-(iii) invariance and horizon-ordering relation with a form-(ii) causal mechanism, constraining what should occur across trajectories, conservation laws, rollout horizons, and dissipative controls; Greydanus et al. (2019) and Cranmer et al. (2020) show why conservation structure is consequential for learned dynamics rather than merely another decodable feature. It establishes both a representational phenomenon and a causally load-bearing mechanism, but a negative result rules out only this linear-direction account—not nonlinear or distributed representations—while true and false remain distinguishable. Topic substitution lowers the assessment from what the importance of scientific representations generally might suggest, but the trajectory invariance plus selective long-versus-short-horizon consequence is specific to this claim and materially sharper than the topic's median decodability hypothesis.

reach.justification: The named handles are the "invariance index" and the "identified invariant direction," usable respectively as a diagnostic and an ablation or steering target. They are primarily post-training and post-hoc because the claim evaluates them against conservation drift already measured in rollouts, rather than asserting a validated forecast of failures before trajectories are attempted. After per-model re-extraction, however, the conclusion predicts a transferable relation—near-constancy within conservative trajectories, variation across initial conditions, selective long-horizon damage after ablation, and absence under friction—rather than merely supplying a search procedure; its asserted scope spans transformers and several classes of classical dynamical systems, with scientific-ML and model-auditing researchers as the main downstream users. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: broad scientific-representation research alone would not earn it, whereas the reusable invariance-and-horizon relation supports reach above the topic median, though not broad deployment or outside-AI uptake.
